newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LAMBERT LIKELY TO BENEFIT FROM FIFA ESTONIA RULING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LAMBERT LIKELY TO BENEFIT FROM FIFA ESTONIA RULING.

text.p: Midfielder Paul Lambert refuses to take comfort from the fact that FIFA's controversial ruling iver Estonia is likely to give him a World Cup reprieve on Sunday.

The Scots must manage their European group four qualifier against Sweden without captain Gary McAllister. He will serve a one-match suspension now that the farcical non-event in Estonia last month cannot be counted as a match played.
Exile Lambert, who plays for Borussia Dortmund, is likely to fill in, but says: "It is a nightmare for Gary and I feel for him.

"If you asked him which match he would rather miss I am sure he'd say the replay with Estonia rather than one against Sweden in front of 50,000 Scotland fans at Ibrox. He's our captain and a tremendous player."
Lambert was one of the Scots who lined up in Tallinn on October 9, for three seconds of action without opposition. But FIFA have ordered the match must be replayed.
"We can't really understand what the thinking has been," said McAllister. "All I can say is that when we go there again we must make sure we beat them and earn the three points."
Fit-again defender Colin Hendry, who missed the trip to Estonia because of injury, will be captain in McAllister's place on Sunday.
Scotland can go top of the group if they win. The Swedes need to shrug off a surprise 1-0 home defeat by Austria.
